Maputo Province Governor Manuel Tule said today, 21 October, in Beluluane, Boane District, that the agreement signed between the National Energy Fund (FUNAE, FP) and Jampur Group, which provides for the Fábrica de Painéis Solares de Moçambique to be placed under private management, will reduce the costs of importing raw materials and promote social inclusion…

signals.title: Ethiopia Calls for Data-Driven Policymaking to Accelerate Africa's Progress
signals.summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Ethiopia has reformed its statistical legislation and established an independent statistical service to strengthen the production and coordination of official data, President Taye Atske Selassie said.

signals.title: Mozambique: Chiquinho Conde announces provisional Mambas squad for AFCON 2027 qualifiers
signals.summary:
Mozambique national football team coach Chiquinho Conde has announced the provisional squad for the Mambas for the FIFA international window from 9 to 17 November 2026, ahead of the third and fourth rounds of the qualifying phase for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON), against Ethiopia. The preliminary list includes players who compete in…

signals.title: Ghana Must Mobilise More Domestic Capital to Finance Economic Growth - Stanbic Ce
signals.summary: [Ghanaian Times] Ghana must strengthen its capacity to mobilise domestic capital to finance economic growth and reduce its exposure to external financial shocks, President of the Ghana Association of Banks and Chief Executive of Stanbic Bank Ghana, Kwamina Asomaning, has said.

signals.title: Can Tanzania Set Its Sights On China's Graphite Crown?
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Tanzania wants to overtake China in graphite production within 15 years. It is a bold target for a country with substantial reserves but only a small share of global output. The announcement signals its intention to become a major force in the fast-growing battery materials market.

signals.title: Livestock Bill Proposes New Fund, Research Agency to Boost Sector
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- The proposed Livestock Bill, 2026, seeks to establish a dedicated fund, new regulatory bodies and a separate research agency to strengthen Kenya's livestock industry, improve market access and increase the value of livestock products.

signals.title: Orchestra Baobab signe son retour avec Made in Senegal
signals.summary: Plus d’un demi-siècle après sa création, Orchestra Baobab s’apprête à publier, le 23 octobre, Made in Senegal, son premier album de compositions inédites en près de dix ans.

signals.title: Ruto Targets Cheaper Mobile Phones Through Proposed Duty Removal
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- President William Ruto has announced plans to pursue the removal of the 25 per cent import duty on mobile phones, in a move aimed at lowering the cost of accessing digital services.

signals.title: L'Éthiopie menace l’Érythrée de "graves conséquences" en cas de soutien aux rebelles
signals.summary: En Éthiopie, le Premier ministre hausse le ton contre l’Érythrée. Abiy Ahmed a mis en garde Asmara contre tout soutien aux groupes rebelles qui combattent le gouvernement fédéral.

signals.title: Will Debt Reforms Unlock Africa's Job Potential?
signals.summary: [Daily News] Dar es Salaam -- THE World Bank International Monetary Fund (IMF) reforms to the Debt Sustainability Framework for Low-Income Countries offer African governments an opportunity to strengthen debt management while protecting resources needed for development and job creation.

signals.title: Bank of Uganda in 100 Percent Surplus Increase Despite Year of Troubles
signals.summary: [Independent (Kampala)] Kampala -- The Bank of Uganda recorded a surplus of 1.32 trillion in the financial year 2025/26, representing a 100 per cent increase from the previous year, while boasting lower than forecast expenditure figures.

signals.title: Ethiopia Signs Second-Phase LNG Development Deal for Ogaden Gas Field
signals.summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Chinese companies GCL Group and Jurong Group have signed an agreement to develop the second phase of a liquefied natural gas (LNG) project at Ethiopia's Calub gas field in the Somali Region, as the government seeks to expand commercial use of the country's natural gas reserves.

signals.title: Mali : Human Rights Watch dénonce des crimes contre les civils [Africanews Today]
signals.summary: Human Rights Watch accuse l'armée, ses alliés russes de l'Africa Corps, mais aussi des groupes armés et jihadistes, d'avoir commis de graves violations du droit international contre des civils. L'ONG appelle à des dispositions urgentes de l'Union africaine.

signals.title: CAN 2025 : le TAS rendra sa décision sur la finale Maroc-Sénégal fin novembre
signals.summary: Le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) a annoncé, lundi 19 octobre, que sa sentence concernant le recours du Sénégal contre le retrait de son titre au profit du Maroc était attendue à la fin du mois de novembre 2026.

signals.title: From Military Victory to Political Settlement - Why Ethiopia's Real Test Lies Beyond Controlling Mekelle
signals.summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Mekelle, the capital of Tigray Regional State, has now changed hands three times in six years. Federal forces took the city in November 2020, within a month of the last war beginning; Tigrayan forces retook it in June 2021. On 3 October 2026, federal troops and the allied Tigray Peace Force entered it again, after the TPLF announced that it had withdrawn and that its regional administration would "temporarily move out" of the capital. The…

signals.title: CAS verdict on Senegal AFCON title appeal 'expected end November'
signals.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced Monday that a verdict on Senegal's appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco will be delivered at the end of November

signals.title: Macky Sall Officially Withdraws His Candidacy for UN Secretary-General Position
signals.summary: [allAfrica] Former Senegalese President Macky Sall announced on Saturday, October 17, 2026, his withdrawal of his candidacy for the post of Secretary-General of the United Nations.

signals.title: Airbus Projects Sixfold Growth in Ethiopia's Air Passenger Traffic Over Next 20 Years
signals.summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- Airbus has forecast a sixfold rise in Ethiopia's air passenger traffic over the next 20 years, saying Ethiopian Airlines is well placed to turn Addis Ababa into one of Africa's leading aviation hubs.

signals.title: Ethiopia, U.S. Treasury Reaffirm Partnership to Deepen Economic Reforms and Bilateral Engagement
signals.summary: [ENA] Addis Ababa -- The Ethiopian high-level delegation met with Eric Meyer, Deputy Assistant Secretary for Africa and the Middle East at the U.S. Department of the Treasury, on the sidelines of the 2026 IMF-World Bank Group Annual Meetings in Bangkok.

signals.title: Canada to Support 200 Mozambican SMEs
signals.summary: [AIM] Maputo -- The Canadian government, through its initiative "Trade for Resilient, Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Growth" (TRISEG), will support 200 Mozambican small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), focusing on strengthening business competitiveness, export capacity, digital transformation and climate resilience.

signals.title: Rwanda to host F1's first race in Africa since 1993
signals.summary: Rwanda signs a 10-year deal with Formula 1 to host races in the African country, starting "in the early 2030s".

signals.title: Cheikhou Kouyaté Announces Retirement From Football
signals.summary: [CAF] Senegalese international midfielder Cheikhou Kouyaté has announced his retirement from professional football at the age of 36, bringing an end to a career defined by his commitment to the national team and Senegal's triumph at the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations Cameroon 2021.

signals.title: BRVM Holds Flat As Bridge Bank Extends Post-Listing Rally
signals.summary: [Daba Finance] The BRVM ended the week to October 9 little changed, with gains in a few stocks offset by declines across most of the market. The Composite index edged up 0.01% to 546.86 points, while the BRVM 30 was unchanged at 264.57 points. The BRVM Prestige rose 0.12% to 203.08 points, while the BRVM Principal fell 1.10% to 379.13 points. Equity market capitalization increased 0.01% to XOF 21.445 trillion.

signals.title: Senegal and Mali Interconnect Their Fiber-Optic Networks
signals.summary: [Daba Finance] Authorities in Senegal and Mali inaugurated the interconnection of their national fiber-optic networks on Monday, October 5. The event took place in Kidira, a strategic border crossing between the two countries. The joint initiative is the result of a collaboration between Sénégal Numérique SA (SENUM SA) and the Malian Transmission and Broadcasting Company (SMTD).

signals.title: Rwanda, Senegal Ink Over 10 Deals to Strengthen Ties
signals.summary: [New Times] Rwanda and Senegal signed 11 cooperation agreements covering areas including development, trade and bilateral relations as the two countries seek to deepen their partnership.

signals.title: 900 Tankers Under Escort - What Africa Corps Actually Does in Mali
signals.summary: [African Arguments] On September 14, 2026, more than 900 fuel tankers entered Bamako under military escort, the Malian government announced. The figure sounds like a victory: the capital got its fuel. But the very need to herd 900 tankers into a single protected convoy is not a story about victory -- it is a story about how vulnerable the ordinary roads have become, the same roads through which Mali imports 95% of its fuel.

signals.title: Eric Muriuki Joins Absa To Lead Pan-African Digital Growth

Eric Muriuki, a former NCBA executive who helped shape some of Kenya’s most prominent mobile-money and digital-lending products, has joined...

signals.title: Aérien : entre Dakar et Abidjan, quelle porte d’entrée pour le Sahel ?
signals.summary: Sur le papier, le retrait des compagnies occidentales du Sahel devrait profiter à Abidjan et Dakar. Mais le report des voyageurs de Bamako, Niamey et Ouagadougou reste limité, tandis qu’Istanbul, Casablanca et Addis-Abeba captent une partie des flux.

signals.title: Mali : les raisons des tensions entre Ismaël Wagué et Sékou Bolly
signals.summary: L’homme d’affaires devenu intermédiaire entre l’État et les groupes armés voit son influence vaciller à Bamako. Derrière ces querelles de cabinet se cachent des rivalités entre généraux, ainsi qu’une féroce bataille pour le contrôle de l’organisation peule Tabital Pulaaku.

signals.title: Only 108 of 39,000 Underage Candidates Meet JAMB Criteria
signals.summary: [Vanguard] Only 108 of about 39,000 underage candidates who sat the 2026 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) have met the Federal Government's screening requirements for possible admission into tertiary institutions.

signals.title: Non-Resident Digital Suppliers Face Uncertainty Over Nigeria's E-Invoicing - Report
signals.summary: [Daily Trust] Non-resident digital service providers operating in Nigeria face uncertainty over compliance with the country's electronic invoicing regime, despite being required to register for Value Added Tax (VAT), charge customers and remit collections to the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS), according to a report by PwC.

signals.title: Imam Removed After Campaigning for Tinubu At Bauchi Mosque
signals.summary: [Daily Trust] Imam Dahiru Abubakar of a mosque in Madina quarters of Bauchi metropolis has been removed from his position for campaigning for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu's re-election.

signals.title: Estará a politica portuguesa à beira do colapso?
signals.summary: Entre o dilema do PS na habitação e o mundo ao contrário no Parlamento, o país anda agitado. Belém chama os partidos e a Defesa avisa: faltam militares para os novos equipamentos.

signals.title: Côte d’Ivoire: audience attendue sur l’élection de Tidjane Thiam à la tête du parti d’opposition PDCI
signals.summary: La justice ivoirienne doit se pencher ce 22 octobre 2026 sur la requête de militants du Parti démocratique de Côte d'Ivoire-Rassemblement démocratique africain (PDCI-RDA) qui veulent faire annuler l’élection en 2025 de Tidjane Thiam à la présidence du PDCI-RDA. Un verdict était attendu le 30 juillet, mais l’audience a finalement été renvoyée à ce jeudi.

signals.title: Nigeria: Lagos built a night economy before it built a nighttime city
signals.summary: Lagos’s nightlife is more than music, clubs and late-night spending – it is a vast, largely overlooked economy that keeps drivers, vendors, hotels and payment platforms busy long after offices close. But as the city’s second shift grows, the infrastructure and policies needed to support it are struggling to keep pace.

signals.title: Ebola - Govt Assures Nigerians of Containment Strategies
signals.summary: [Presidency Nigeria] The Presidential Task Force on Ebola Preparedness, Virus Disease Preparedness and Emerging Public Health Threats has assured Nigerians it can handle Ebola in the country.

signals.title: Film On Abduction of 67 Children to Premiere in Abuja, Targets Public Apathy Towards Insecurity
signals.summary: [This Day] Abuja -- A Nigerian film series centred on the abduction of 67 children will premiere in Abuja next week, with its creators seeking to turn public outrage over insecurity into sustained civic action and pressure for accountability.

signals.title: Ekiti Assembly Passes Bill to Establish State Police
signals.summary: [Premium Times] The bill scaled second and third readings during plenary, with all 21 members present supporting its passage, signalling the Assembly's endorsement of the proposed constitutional framework for decentralised policing.

signals.title: Kaduna Police DPO Detains Female Journalist, Parents Over N100 Dispute
signals.summary: [Premium Times] Usman Adamu, the divisional police officer (DPO) of Mararaban Jos in Kaduna State, has detained a young female journalist, Farida Isiak, and her parents, following a dispute between her mother and a neighbour over the sale of charcoal.

signals.title: Sanwo-Olu Warns Against Wetland Destruction, Strengthens Plastic Ban Enforcement
signals.summary: [This Day] Lagos residents face mounting environmental risks as the state generates about 13,000 tonnes of waste daily, with plastics accounting for 15 per cent, Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has warned, linking indiscriminate waste disposal and wetland destruction to worsening floods, damaged property and threats to public health.

signals.title: Le Ghana veut interdire les exportations de matières premières d’ici à 2030
signals.summary: À l'occasion du sommet Afrique du Financial Times à Londres, le président ghanéen a fait plusieurs déclarations mercredi 21 octobre, notamment en annonçant son souhait d’arrêter les exportations de matières premières d’ici à 2030. John Dramani Mahama cherche à développer la transformation locale de ces minerais, soit un changement de stratégie dans la région.

signals.title: Single Opposition Candidate - Atiku, Obi, Duke, Others Discussing, Says Lukman-Led Coalition
signals.summary: [Leadership] The opposition leaders on the platform of the G-100 coalition yesterday declared that the quest to produce a consensus presidential candidate to challenge President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election has made significant progress.

signals.title: Nigeria Has Measures in Place to Contain Ebola - Pate
signals.summary: [Leadership] The Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, has assured Nigerians that the federal government has put measures in place to contain a reported imported case of Ebola and prevent its spread within the country.

signals.title: MPs Query Water Ministry's Advance Payments to Contractors
signals.summary: [Nile Post] Members of Parliament on the Public Accounts Committee - Central Government have questioned the Ministry of Water and Environment over advance payments to contractors before project sites are handed over and construction begins, raising concerns about accountability and the management of public funds.

signals.title: Tanzania Advises Africa to Rely On Domestic Funding to Explore, Process, Refine Its Minerals
signals.summary: [Daily News] Accra -- THE Minister for Minerals, Anthony Mavunde has called upon African nations to mobilise domestic resources to finance mineral exploration, processing and refining instead of relying heavily on foreign funding.

signals.title: Government Moves to Tighten Noose On Illicit Alcohol Cartels
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Deputy President Kithure Kindiki has declared illicit alcohol a major threat to Kenya's future, warning that the government will introduce tougher laws and intensify enforcement to dismantle networks involved in the production and sale of harmful alcoholic drinks.

signals.title: Matiang'i, Karua and Nyoro Rally Opposition Support in Njoro Ahead of 2027 Polls
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nakuru -- Opposition leaders Fred Matiang'i, Martha Karua and Ndindi Nyoro have vowed to unite behind a single presidential candidate to challenge President William Ruto in the August 2027 General Election.

signals.title: Man Jailed for Seven Years Over Pangolin Scales Worth Sh300,000
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- A man has been sentenced to seven years in prison for dealing in pangolin scales valued at Sh300,000 in Taveta, Taita-Taveta County.

signals.title: Kindiki, Kingi, Khaminwa Among 146 Lawyers Seeking Senior Counsel Rank
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Deputy President Kithure Kindiki, Senate Speaker Amason Kingi, former National Assembly Speaker Kenneth Marende and veteran lawyer John Khaminwa are among 146 advocates seeking conferment of the prestigious rank of Senior Counsel in the 2026 selection cycle.

signals.title: Who Protects the Protectors? Inside the Growing Danger for Ethiopia's Humanitarian Workers
signals.summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- When humanitarian workers travel to the field, they carry more than food, medicine, or information. They carry the hopes of people facing hunger, displacement, illness, and conflict. Yet, the danger increasingly exposes those delivering this assistance.

signals.title: Entrenched Authoritarianism: Ethiopia's Rule of Law Index Slides Further
signals.summary: [Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Ethiopia's rule of law performance has deteriorated further, with the country ranking 133rd out of 143 countries and jurisdictions in the 2026 World Justice Project (WJP) Rule of Law Index, according to the ranking provided for this report. The latest assessment extends a multi-year decline that has seen the country remain near the bottom of global and sub-Saharan African comparisons.

signals.title: MP Mogaka Backs Ruto, Cites Development Projects in West Mugirango
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- West Mugirango MP Stephen Mogaka has declared support for President William Ruto's administration, citing ongoing development projects in his constituency as the main reason for his political shift.

signals.title: Major General Julius Osifo Assumes Office As MPB Chairman, Pledges Prompt Payment of Military Pensions
signals.summary: [This Day] Major General Julius Ehioze Osifo has assumed office as Chairman of the Military Pensions Board (MPB), pledging to ensure prompt, seamless and less bureaucratic payment of pensions, gratuities, arrears and death benefits to retired and discharged military personnel and families of deceased service members.

signals.title: Senate Mourns Uduaghan, Recalls Role in Niger Delta Amnesty, Regional Integration
signals.summary: [This Day] Senate, yesterday, paid tribute to former governor of Delta State, Emmanuel Uduaghan, recalling his contributions to peace-building in the Niger Delta, regional economic integration, and the development of healthcare and infrastructure during his eight-year administration.

signals.title: Govt, States, Agencies Rally Nigerians in Early Fight Against Ebola
signals.summary: [This Day] The federal government, state governments, the National Assembly and public health institutions yesterday intensified efforts to prevent the spread of Ebola in Nigeria, mobilising health workers, strengthening disease surveillance and urging Nigerians to adopt precautionary measures following confirmation of an imported case in Abuja.

signals.title: Immigration CG Warns Officers Against Corruption, Vows Sanctions
signals.summary: [Daily Trust] The Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS), Kemi Nandap, has warned officers against corruption and abuse of official processes, saying anyone found culpable will face the full weight of the law.

signals.title: Nigeria 2027: Can Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour break Tinubu’s 27-year grip on Lagos?
signals.summary: After losing the 2023 governorship race, the opposition politician is preparing for another showdown with Bola Tinubu’s powerful political machine. Now in the ADC party, he explains why he believes he can succeed where others have failed.

signals.title: The Palace Guard Against the Trenches - What the Mutiny in Niamey Revealed
signals.summary: [African Arguments] The mutiny that broke out in air base 101 in Niamey in the night of 29 August 2026 failed. The real question now is to understand why it took place. Those who took up arms against General Abdourahamane Tiani were young soldiers from the front lines, those who fought the 'jihadists.' For all of the Sahel, it's a much more worrying sign than any plot from the army high command.

signals.title: Madagascar: le Pôle anti-corruption suspend ses poursuites contre l’ex-président Andry Rajoelina et ses ministres
signals.summary: À Madagascar, la justice suspend trois grandes affaires de corruption de l’ancien régime. Elles visent l’ex-président Andry Rajoelina, son ancien Premier ministre Christian Ntsay et plusieurs anciens ministres. Le tribunal chargé de les juger, le Pôle anti-corruption, souhaite confirmer qu'il est habilité à les juger.

signals.title: Sénégal: la grève générale se poursuit, les syndicats se félicitent d'une première journée «bien suivie»
signals.summary: À quelques jours seulement des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse qui s'ouvriront le 31 octobre dans le pays, le Front syndical pour la défense du travail, une plateforme qui réunit 13 centrales syndicales, appelle les Sénégalais à trois jours de mobilisation pour améliorer leurs conditions de travail dans différents secteurs. Commencé mercredi, le mouvement doit durer jusqu'au vendredi 23 octobre.

signals.title: Tchad: l'ancien Premier ministre Succès Masra a quitté le pays pour recevoir des soins
signals.summary: Parti dans le 20 octobre en toute discrétion deux mois après sa libération au bénéfice d'une grâce présidentielle, celui-ci doit rejoindre la France après avoir transité par le Cameroun et la Côte d'Ivoire, où se trouve sa famille. « Ce n’est pas un nouvel exil ! », précise l'un de ses collaborateurs.

signals.title: Tigray resumes daily life amid fears of wider war
signals.summary: Mekelle’s reopening offers little relief as instability and economic hardship persist.

signals.title: Guinée: quelles alternatives au sachet d'eau bientôt interdit?
signals.summary: En Guinée, l'interdiction des plastiques à usage unique, dont les sachets d'eau très bon marché, provoque une crise d'accès à l'eau potable. Un moratoire de six mois est accordé pour trouver des alternatives conciliant santé et environnement, tandis que les autorités et les industriels peinent à résoudre l'équation entre besoins essentiels de la population et lutte contre la pollution.

signals.title: «On s'appelle, on s'entraide»: au Sénégal, des malades du cancer du sein unies contre la maladie
signals.summary: À l'occasion d'Octobre rose, mois de mobilisation contre le cancer du sein, rendez-vous au Sénégal, où les malades n'ont pas accès aux soins de support comme un accompagnement psychologique et social pour lutter contre l'isolement, l'anxiété, la dépression. À Dakar, l'association Kinsiba propose des cours de boxe ou encore des séances de henné entre femmes, pour redonner confiance et briser la solitude.

signals.title: Nigeria's first Ebola patient holidayed in Uganda, officials say
signals.summary: The wife of a diplomat based in Abuja travelled to Kampala for a vacation.

signals.title: Owebeyi to Appeal Court Ruling Dismissing Bukimbiri Election Petition
signals.summary: [Nile Post] Former Forum for Democratic Change (FDC) parliamentary candidate James Owebeyi has said he will appeal a High Court decision dismissing his petition challenging the election of Bukimbiri County MP Eddie Kwizera Wagahungu.

signals.title: Kabale Gives Science Kits to 20 Primary Schools to Boost CBC
signals.summary: [Nile Post] Kabale District has handed over 20 science kits, also known as mini-laboratories, to 20 government-aided primary schools to support the implementation of the Competency-Based Curriculum (CBC).

signals.title: Mityana Health Workers Warn of Eye Problems Among Students
signals.summary: [Nile Post] Health workers in Mityana District have urged parents and schools to promote healthier lifestyles among learners amid concerns about eye problems and non-communicable diseases among students.

signals.title: Government Moves to Return Fisheries Management to Fishermen
signals.summary: [Nile Post] The government plans to return some fisheries management responsibilities to fishermen through landing site committees, in a shift from an enforcement system that has relied heavily on the military to police fishing activities.

signals.title: Niger : deux otages occidentales libérées en Libye après plus d’un an et demi aux mains de l’État islamique
signals.summary: Détenues au Niger par l’État islamique pendant plus d’un an et demi, Claudia Abbt et Eva Gretzmacher ont été libérées et sont arrivées à Benghazi. La médiation a été orchestrée par Saddam Haftar, désireux d’asseoir son influence politique au Sahel.

signals.title: Éthiopie : Abiy Ahmed, la guerre permanente
signals.summary: Couronné du Nobel de la paix en 2019, le Premier ministre éthiopien fait face à une nouvelle escalade militaire. Entre tensions avec l’Érythrée et rebellions internes, il s’enfonce dans une logique de guerre pour maintenir son pouvoir.

signals.title: Burundi : hommage à Melchior Ndadaye, 33 ans après son assassinat
signals.summary: Le Burundi a commémoré, mercredi 21 octobre, le 33e anniversaire de l’assassinat de Melchior Ndadaye, premier président démocratiquement élu du pays. À Bujumbura, les cérémonies ont été marquées par des dépôts de gerbes et des appels à renforcer la démocratie.

signals.title: Sénégal : une grève paralyse plusieurs secteurs à l’approche des JOJ
signals.summary: 🇸🇳 Au Sénégal, une grève générale de trois jours a débuté ce mercredi, à l’appel du Front syndical pour la défense du travail. La mobilisation rassemble treize syndicats de l’éducation, des transports. Le gouvernement a appelé les travailleurs à renoncer à cette grève "illégale".

signals.title: Burkina, Mali, Guinée… Le pari de la reprise en main de l’or porte-t-il ses fruits ?
signals.summary: Raffineries, nouvelles règles d’exportation, compagnies minières publiques… Les gouvernements d’Afrique de l’Ouest multiplient les mesures pour reprendre le contrôle de leur filière aurifère. Reste encore à prouver que ces initiatives sont efficaces.

signals.title: Burundi marks 33 years since Ndadaye’s assassination amid concerns over democracy
signals.summary: Burundi has commemorated the 33rd anniversary of the assassination of former President Melchior Ndadaye, with tributes to the slain leader renewing debate over the state of democracy in the country.

signals.title: Prioritise Ethical Reporting to Protect Country's Financial Stability - BoG Urges Financial Journalists
signals.summary: [Ghanaian Times] The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has urged financial journalists to prioritise ethical journalism and ensure accuracy, fairness and balance in their reporting to protect the country's financial stability and prevent misinformation from undermining public confidence in the economy.

signals.title: Abena Amoah Crowned CIMG Marketing Woman of the Year
signals.summary: [Ghanaian Times] The Managing Director of the Ghana Stock Exchange (GSE), Ms Abena Amoah, has been adjudged the Marketing Woman of the Year 2025 by the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG), in recognition of her contribution to marketing and leadership in the country's financial sector.

signals.title: Police Coordinate Search for Missing Fishing Canoe and Seven Crew Members
signals.summary: [Ghanaian Times] The Western Regional Marine Police Command is collaborating with the Ghana Navy, Ghana Maritime Authority (GMA), Fisheries Commission and fishing communities to locate a missing fishing canoe and its seven crew members.

signals.title: GAF Staff Wins Tampico Accra Inter-City Marathon
signals.summary: [Ghanaian Times] Ishmael Arthur of the Ghana Armed Forces (GAF) emerged the winner of the 2026 Tampico Accra Inter-City Marathon with a time of 1:10:44.97 in the men's 21-kilometre category, beating off competition from over 1,000 participants.

signals.title: Ghana Secures Qualification for 2026 Beach Soccer AFCON .
signals.summary: [Ghanaian Times] Ghana's national beach soccer team, the Black Sharks, have booked their ticket to the 2026 CAF Beach Soccer Africa Cup of Nations in Senegal after securing a commanding 7-4 victory over arch-rivals Nigeria in the final round of qualifiers.

signals.title: Former GPL Sides to Headline MTN FA Cup Prelims Games
signals.summary: [Ghanaian Times] Matches involving four former Ghana Premier League (GPL) clubs would headline the preliminary round of Ghana's second-tier club football competition, the MTN FA Cup, which is expected to kick-start from October 23.

signals.title: Ghana in talks with European nations for reparations, president says
signals.summary: John Mahama says efforts are focused on securing the return of artefacts stolen during the centuries of the slave trade and colonialism

signals.title: CAS to Rule On AFCON Final Case Next Month
signals.summary: [Ghanaian Times] A decision on Senegal's appeal after being stripped of this year's Africa Cup of Nations title will be made at the end of November, the Court of Arbitration for Sport said yesterday.

Mali's Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Minister, Abdoulaye Diop, used his address to the United Nations General Debate to defend the country's growing focus on strategic autonomy and its partnership with Burkina Faso and Niger.

signals.title: Mali Army and Russian Fighters Accused of Killing Dozens of Civilians
signals.summary: [RFI] Mali's armed forces and Russian Wagner Group personnel committed war crimes including killings and torture of civilians during joint operations between 2023 and 2025, Amnesty International has said in a new report documenting abuses across several regions of the country.

signals.title: Afcon 27 Qualifiers - Nigeria Thrashed, Rwanda Stay Perfect As Vieira Picks First Senegal Win
signals.summary: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Nigeria suffered a 3-0 thrashing at the hands of Guinea Bissau in their second match of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations last night.

signals.title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute
signals.summary: Kijanangoma has been crowned amid a dispute over a young heir whom the royal clan does not recognise.

signals.title: The journalist who became king in Uganda
signals.summary: Edward Rukidi Nyabongo I has been crowned king of Tooro in a ceremony attended by Uganda's President Museveni.

signals.title: Historian Hassoum Ceesay Says Gambia-Senegal Border Has Not Been Demarcated Since 1904-05
signals.summary: [Foroyaa] There has been no formal boundary demarcation exercise between The Gambia and Senegal for more than a century, according to Hassoum Ceesay, Director General of the National Centre for Arts and Culture (NCAC).

signals.title: Black Maidens Beat Cote d'Ivoire in Final Wafu B Cup Contest
signals.summary: [Ghanaian Times] The Black Maidens ended their WAFU B U-17 Girls Cup campaign with an emphatic 4-0 victory over hosts Cote d'Ivoire on Sunday.

signals.title: Damning Evidence of War Crimes By State Armed Forces and Wagner Group Personnel - New Report
signals.summary: [AI London] Killings of civilians during military joint operations Civilians tortured to death in detention, others subjected to simulated drowning, beatings and electric shocks Fulani, Arabs and Tuaregs targeted

signals.title: UNGA81 - Nigeria, Mali Discuss Sahel Security
signals.summary: [Daily Trust] Nigeria and Mali have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral relations and enhancing cooperation in addressing security and development challenges confronting the Sahel and West Africa.

signals.title: Group-by-Group - How the AFCON PAMOJA 2027 Qualifying Race Stands After Matchday One
signals.summary: [CAF] Morocco, Côte d'Ivoire, Algeria, Nigeria and Cameroon were among the continental heavyweights to make winning starts as the first matchday of the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations PAMOJA 2027 qualifiers produced goals, comebacks and several away successes across Africa.

signals.title: Zimbabwe Produce Stunning Comeback As Cameroon and Cote d'Ivoire Open With Wins
signals.summary: [CAF] Zimbabwe produced the most dramatic result of Thursday night's TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations 2027 qualifiers, recovering from two goals down to beat Sierra Leone 3-2.

signals.title: Guinea-Bissau Stun Tanzania As Mozambique Deny Vieira Winning Senegal Start
signals.summary: [CAF] Guinea-Bissau produced the standout result of Friday's early TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations 2027 qualifiers with a 2-0 away victory over co-hosts Tanzania.

signals.title: Ghana, Cote d'Ivoire Reaffirm 150km Boundary
signals.summary: [Ghanaian Times] Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire have completed the first phase of a joint exercise to reaffirm their 150-kilometre international land boundary with the inauguration of 37 new boundary pillars.

signals.title: Bridge Bank Jumps 16 Percent in BRVM Debut Amid Broad Market Decline
signals.summary: [Daba Finance] Bridge Bank Group Côte d'Ivoire (BRVM: BBGC) gained 15.48% in its first 2 trading sessions on the BRVM, making it the exchange's best-performing stock in the week ended September 25 even as the broader market fell. The shares closed at XOF 7,795, compared with an IPO reference price of XOF 6,750.

signals.title: Senegal's President Faye - Macky Sall Best Candidate 'To Fight for Africa' At UN
signals.summary: [RFI] Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has thrown his weight behind his predecessor and former political rival Macky Sall to become the next United Nations secretary-general. No one is better placed to fight for Africa's place at the table, he told RFI and France 24.

signals.title: Afcon 2027 Qualifier in Bouake - Black Stars Face Cote d'Ivoire's Elephants...Without 7 Key Players
signals.summary: [Ghanaian Times] The Black Stars of Ghana will begin their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) journey today with a tough test in Bouaké, where they face The Elephants of La Côte d'Ivoire without several key players.

signals.title: Senegal Reaffirms Support for Morocco's Position On Sahara Dispute
signals.summary: [New Republic] Senegal's Minister of African Integration, Foreign Affairs and Senegalese Abroad, Cheikh Niang, has reaffirmed Senegal's position that the Sahara is Moroccan, calling for "realism" in efforts to reach a lasting solution to the regional dispute.

signals.title: Black Stars Touch Down in Bouaké Ahead of Crunch Afcon Qualifier Against Côte d'Ivoire
signals.summary: [Ghanaian Times] The Black Stars of Ghana have arrived in Côte d'Ivoire ahead of their highly anticipated Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifier clash against the Elephants of Côte d'Ivoire.

signals.title: Watch: Why is the UK reviewing its Chagos Islands deal?
signals.summary: The UK is reviewing its deal to hand over the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, the defence secretary has said.

signals.title: There's No Conspiracy in the Sahel - - There's a Gap, and Bamako Knows How to Use It
signals.summary: [African Arguments] A familiar claim keeps surfacing in the rhetoric of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger's ruling juntas, echoed enthusiastically by Russian state media: the West is deliberately working to destabilise the Sahel's military governments. It's a tidy story. It bundles sanctions, frozen aid and diplomatic isolation into a single narrative of conspiracy. But look closely at who is actually doing what, and what looks like a strategy of destabilisation turns out to…

signals.title: Inside Djibouti refugee camp for thousands fleeing Houthi advance in Yemen
signals.summary: Fighting on Yemen's west coast has prompted thousands of people to flee by boat across the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
